153846334.title: File:Notice of investigation into the sexual behaviour of Sanzo Tsuda (Tsuda Sanzō), Japanese police record of the Ōtsu incident, 13 May 1891.jpg

ObjectName.value: Notice of investigation into the sexual behaviour of Sanzo Tsuda (Tsuda Sanzō), Japanese police record of the Ōtsu incident, 13 May 1891

Categories.value: Ōtsu incident|PD-Art (PD-old-70)|PD-Art (PD-old default)|CC-PD-Mark|PD-Art missing SDC copyright status|PD-old missing SDC copyright status

ImageDescription.value:
Notice of investigation into the sexual behaviour of Sanzo Tsuda (Tsuda Sanzō), Japanese police record of the Ōtsu incident, 13 May 1891.

3: Two days after the incident, the Prefectural Police Department ordered each police chief to investigate police officers under their jurisdiction who had been in contact with Sanzo Tsuda, and to report on Tsuda's behavior. The order included information on Tsuda's "lifestyle, wealth and poverty," his favorite newspapers and magazines, his drinking habits, and his belief in Shintoism and Buddhism. Order 4-6822-5(1)]【令4-6822-5(1)】

The Otsu Incident Traced from Police Documents: On May 11, 1891, Officer Sanzo Tsuda, who was on guard duty, slashed Russian Crown Prince Nikolai, who was visiting Otsu. This was the "Otsu Incident. This record is one of the materials related to the Otsu Incident that were transferred from the National Police Headquarters to the National Archives of Japan in 2022.
